quotes: LeakGuard runs under its own service account svc-leakguard.
The account is not used by any staff member.
findings.model_reasoning: These sentences show the agent uses its own service account and that staff do not use that account. That supports separation from any staff login.

quotes: For pump scheduling, svc-leakguard may change schedules only for pumps at the Hillside station, within the pressure limits set by staff.
findings.model_reasoning: The quoted scope limits the account to specific pump-scheduling actions and excludes other actions, which shows restricted permissions. The limits are described in the access register, showing the permissions are being reviewed/controlled.

quotes: Maria, operations lead, approves pump schedule changes proposed by LeakGuard.
She can override or stop any change from the control-room console.
findings.model_reasoning: This names a person with authority to approve, override, and stop the agent’s actions. The procedure states this control clearly.

quotes: A schedule change can be reverted to the previous schedule with one command.
findings.model_reasoning: This shows the action can be reversed. The quote also indicates a quick manual recovery path through a single command.

quotes: Every LeakGuard action is written to the central log with time, account, action, target and result.
findings.model_reasoning: This sentence states that every action is logged automatically and includes the required fields: time, agent identity via account, action, target, and result.

quotes: We have not yet decided how long to keep the LeakGuard logs.
findings.model_reasoning: The evidence explicitly says the retention period has not yet been decided, so there is no support for six-month retention. There is also no evidence that the logs are reviewed.
The evidence does not mention any incident plan for agent malfunction or misuse, nor any NIS2 reporting deadlines. The only incident-related note says the vendor contract has no notification clause.

quotes: The vendor contract is still being negotiated and has no clause on notifying us of incidents.
findings.model_reasoning: This directly shows there is no contract clause requiring vendor incident notification. The evidence also does not mention vulnerability notification.
